Subject: Deployment mode qualification: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (HIPAA/SOC2) - Acme Health

Hi Sara / Tom,

Thanks again for taking the time today — appreciated the walkthrough of Acme Health's clinical triage workflow and the security requirements. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment on deployment mode and compliance asks.

Summary of requirements I captured:
- PHI will be processed (patient names, DOB, limited clinical notes) during the PoC and production runs.
- BAA signed before production; SOC2 Type II evidence required for procurement.
- Encryption at rest + customer-managed keys (KMS/HSM) for production-grade deployments.
- Audit logs and retention: ability to pull access/audit logs for up to 12 months for audits.
- Network isolation preference: your team mentioned preference for VPC/private deployment for production but open to Dedicated for initial PoC depending on timing.

Deployment mode considerations (high level):
- Hosted API: fastest to onboard, supports BAA + SOC2 controls. Default for many PoCs but runs on our shared control plane.
- Dedicated: reserved GPU pools and tenant isolation (good middle ground). Provides stronger isolation, predictable capacity, configurable autoscaling.
- Private (VPC / on-prem): customer-managed networking, optional on-prem package, full KMS/HSM integrations, recommended when an auditor requires tenant network isolation or you need full control of networking.

Attachments I will share in the next email: Redwood SOC2 Type II report (redacted) and our standard BAA draft.

Proposed next steps:
1) I’ll share SOC2 report + BAA draft (attachment) — please confirm receipt.
2) Schedule a technical deep-dive with Marissa (solutions) and Dylan (infra) to validate KMS, audit logs, and exact retention/audit requirements — suggested slots below.
3) If you need private VPC for production, we can surface onboarding checklist and procurement requirements ahead of the call.

Suggested times for a 60-min tech call (all times ET):

- Tue 7/21, 3:00pm-4:00pm ET
- Wed 7/22, 1:00pm-2:00pm ET

If you prefer a different cadence, tell me what works and I’ll get it on the calendar.

Thanks — Neha

[Attachment: Redwood_SOC2_Report_Q2_2026.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)]
[Attachment: Standard_BAA_Redwood_v1.docx (DOCX, 48KB)]

Quick answers to your questions:
- SOC2 scope & date: the attached report is SOC2 Type II covering controls operating from 2025-01-01 through 2026-03-31. It includes infrastructure and encryption controls relevant to data-at-rest and key management.
- Encryption & KMS: we support AES-256 encryption at rest. For Hosted and Dedicated we manage keys by default; for Private VPC/on-prem we support customer-managed KMS and HSM integrations (bring-your-own-key).
- Audit logs & retention: audit logs (access, admin, model invocation metadata) can be exported to your S3/GCS endpoint and retained for 12+ months. We also offer a log-retention add-on for longer-term archival and an exports API for ad-hoc audits.
- BAA: attached is our standard BAA. We can accept reasonably scoped redlines and have a standard workflow for counter-signing via DocuSign.

Recommendation on deployment mode based on your notes:
- PoC: Dedicated is often the fastest path if you want stronger isolation without full VPC onboarding (reserved capacity, isolated GPU pools).
- Production: Private VPC is the recommended option when an auditor requires tenant network isolation or you need customer-managed KMS/HSM and stricter network controls.

I’ve added a short matrix here:
- Hosted API: Fastest, BAA + SOC2 compliant for many customers, shared control plane.
- Dedicated: Tenant isolation, reserved capacity, good mid-ground for early Prod.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): Full network isolation, customer KMS, best for regulated production and audit requirements.

Next steps:
